source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 103:1-22 . A Psalm of joyous praise, in which the writer rises from a thankful acknowledgment of personal blessings to a lively celebration of God's gracious attributes, as not only intrinsically worthy of praise, but as specially suited to man's frailty. He concludes by invoking all creatures to unite in his song.

entries.heading: 2. forget not all
entries.text: 2. forget not all --not any, none of His benefits.

entries.heading: 4. redeemeth
entries.text: 4. redeemeth --Cost is implied. destruction --literally, "pit of corruption" ( Ps 16:10 ). crowneth --or, "adorneth" ( Ps 65:11 ). tender mercies --compassions (compare Ps 25:6; 40:11 ).
5. By God's provision, the saint retains a youthful vigor like the eagles ( Ps 92:14 ; compare Isa 40:31 ).
6. Literally, "righteousness and judgments," denoting various acts of God's government.

entries.heading: 7. ways
entries.text: 7. ways --of providence, &c., as usual ( Ps 25:4; 67:2 ). acts --literally, "wonders" ( Ps 7:11; 78:17 ).
8-10. God's benevolence implies no merit. He shows it to sinners, who also are chastened for a time ( Ex 34:6 ). keep (anger) --in Le 19:18 , bear a grudge ( Jer 3:5, 12 ).

entries.heading: 12. removed . . . from us
entries.text: 12. removed . . . from us --so as no longer to affect our relations to Him.

entries.heading: 14. he
entries.text: 14. he --"who formed," Ps 94:9 . knoweth our frame --literally, "our form." we are dust --made of and tending to it ( Ge 2:7 ).
15, 16. So short and frail is life that a breath may destroy it. it is gone --literally, "it is not." know it no more --no more recognize him ( Ps 90:6; Isa 40:6-8 ).

entries.heading: 18. such . . . covenant
entries.text: 18. such . . . covenant --limits the general terms preceding. righteousness --as usual ( Ps 7:17; 31:1 ).
19. God's firm and universal dominion is a pledge that He will keep His promises ( Ps 11:4; 47:8 ).

entries.heading: 20-22. do his commandments . . . word
entries.text: 20-22. do his commandments . . . word --or, literally, "so as to hearken," &c., that is, their acts of obedience are prompt, so that they are ever ready to hear, and know, and follow implicitly His declared will (compare De 26:17; Lu 1:19 ).

entries.heading: 21. ye his hosts
entries.text: 21. ye his hosts --myriads, or armies, as corresponding to angels of great power [ Ps 103:20 ], denoting multitudes also.

entries.heading: 22. all his works
entries.text: 22. all his works --creatures of every sort, everywhere.
